spec: Schedule [arrive, depart, tons] vessels sequentially against tonnage_cap (>= 0, else ValueError; depart > arrive and tons >= 0, else ValueError). Release accepted vessels with prev_depart <= arrive before checking active_tons + tons <= tonnage_cap; return [accepted_booleans, peak_active_tons].

Given segments [kind, length] (kind in ('data', 'meta'), length >= 0, else ValueError) and query [offset, offset + span) (offset >= 0, span >= 0, else ValueError), advance logical payload offset only on 'data' segments and return overlap byte counts for each 'data' segment in order.

Over integer window [open_hr, close_hr) with close_hr > open_hr (else ValueError), clip each [start_hr, end_hr, rate] booking with end_hr > start_hr to [open_hr, close_hr) and add rate to each covered hour slot; return the per-hour load list of length close_hr - open_hr.

Process [op, escrow_id, amount] records: 'open' opens inactive escrow_id at 0, 'credit' adds integer amount to open escrow_id, 'release' closes open escrow_id and appends [escrow_id, balance], 'void' closes open escrow_id without emitting (any invalid state transition or unknown op raises ValueError; closed IDs may reopen fresh).

Process [kind, sensor_id, value] items: 'sample' emits 0 on first reading for sensor_id in its current epoch (setting high = value), otherwise if value > high emits value - high and updates high = value else emits 0 without lowering high; 'recal' resets only sensor_id so its next sample starts a fresh epoch (unknown kind raises ValueError).

Process [tag, delta] steps: 'step' adds delta to level and updates stage_min over post-step levels in the current stage; 'pause' resets level to 0 while keeping stage_min; 'close' appends stage_min (or None if no 'step' occurred in the stage) and resets both level and stage_min.

Given stock dict {sku: count} (counts >= 0, else ValueError) and sequential baskets (each a list of [sku, qty] lines with qty >= 1, else ValueError, possibly repeating sku within a basket), atomically deduct a basket iff total per-sku demand fits remaining stock, returning total remaining stock across all skus after accepted baskets or -1 for rejected baskets.

Given [ward, candidate] ballots and min_wards >= 1 (else ValueError), count distinct non-empty wards endorsing each non-empty candidate (ignoring rows with empty ward or candidate) and return [candidate, ward_count] sorted by descending ward_count then ascending candidate.

Given left_rows and right_rows of [key, team, weight], return [pair_count, weight_sum] over all index pairs (left_idx, right_idx) with matching key and distinct team (left_team != right_team), summing left_weight + right_weight for each qualifying index pair.

Maintain a queue of capacity limit >= 1 (else ValueError) over [cmd, job] commands: 'push' moves job to newest if already queued (without dropping anything), else appends job after dropping and recording oldest if len == limit; 'pop' removes and ignores oldest if non-empty. Return [dropped_jobs, remaining_oldest_to_newest].

Given [actor, valid_flag, points] logs (valid_flag in (0, 1), else ValueError), sum points across valid (valid_flag == 1) logs per actor; invalid logs neither contribute points nor establish first-valid index. Return [actor, total_points] for actors with >= 1 valid log sorted by descending total_points then earliest valid log index.

Given proposals [title, dept, priority, cost] (cost >= 0, else ValueError) and dept_budgets {dept: budget} (budgets >= 0, else ValueError), greedily accept proposals in descending priority order (ties by earlier index) whenever cost <= remaining dept budget (missing dept has budget 0), then return accepted titles in original input index order.

Start door in 'closed' state over commands in ('open', 'close', 'lock', 'unlock') (else ValueError). Valid transitions: closed->open on 'open', open->closed on 'close' (incrementing cycles), closed->locked on 'lock', locked->closed on 'unlock'; other commands in valid set are ignored without changing state. Return [final_state, cycles].

Decode integer byte values (each 0..255, else ValueError): in normal mode 254 enters escape mode (next byte XOR 32 appended, returning to normal) and 255 enters pair-sum mode (next two bytes summed modulo 256 and appended, returning to normal); other bytes append directly. Dangling incomplete escape or pair-sum at end raises ValueError.

Simulate outcomes in ('ok', 'temp', 'fatal') with 1 <= base_delay <= max_delay (else ValueError), starting cur_delay = base_delay: 'ok' increments ok_count and resets cur_delay = base_delay (adding 0 wait); 'temp' adds cur_delay to total_wait and updates cur_delay = min(max_delay, cur_delay * 2); 'fatal' stops processing immediately without adding wait. Return [ok_count, total_wait].

Given integer list values and window width >= 1 (else ValueError), return for each contiguous window values[idx : idx + width] the count of elements whose frequency inside that window is strictly 1 (empty list if len(values) < width).

Given integer list nums, tolerance >= 0, and max_len >= 1 (else ValueError), count contiguous nonempty subarrays nums[left : right + 1] with length <= max_len and max(subarray) - min(subarray) <= tolerance.

With integer weight in 1..10 (else ValueError), initialize integer EMA avg = samples[0] on index 0 and update avg = (weight * sample + (10 - weight) * avg) // 10 for subsequent samples; a sample breaches when post-update avg > hi_mark. Return [max_consecutive_breaches, total_breaches].

Validate [kind, tag] tokens (kind in ('open', 'close', 'self'), non-empty tag, max_depth >= 1, else ValueError): 'open' pushes tag (invalid if new depth > max_depth), 'self' requires len(stack) + 1 <= max_depth (recording transient depth len(stack) + 1 without staying open), 'close' requires non-empty stack with top == tag; stop immediately on first structural violation and return [is_valid, peak_valid_depth].

Given list symbols with each item in ('(', ')', '[', ']') (else ValueError), process left-to-right maintaining an open-opener stack: an opener pushes onto the stack; a closer pops the top if non-empty and matching ('()' or '[]'), otherwise leaves the stack unchanged and increments closer_repairs (requiring one inserted matching opener immediately before it). At end, remaining unclosed openers on the stack add len(stack) to opener_repairs. Return [closer_repairs, opener_repairs].

Given profiler trace [kind, func_name, timestamp] (kind in ('enter', 'exit'), non-empty func_name, non-decreasing non-negative timestamps, matching LIFO exits, and empty stack at end, else ValueError), compute exclusive execution time per function (pausing caller time while callee runs) and return [func_name, exclusive_time] sorted by func_name.

Given [label, delta] runs (non-empty label, integer delta, else ValueError), skip zero deltas and merge adjacent runs having the same label by summing delta; if a merged run reaches sum 0, remove it so newly adjacent runs can also merge! Return surviving [label, net_delta] runs.

Given streams (list of [pkg, version] lists, non-empty pkg, else ValueError), ignore entries with version < 0, establish each qualifying pkg position by its earliest non-negative appearance across streams in order, and retain the maximum non-negative version observed for that pkg.

Given sorted_lists (each a non-decreasing integer list, else ValueError) and min_lists >= 1 (else ValueError), return a strictly increasing list of integers that appear in at least min_lists distinct input lists (deduplicating repeats within the same input list).
